title: The rebalancing run record read on the rwb-case contract is not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6, FSD P3 A2.17; Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD P3 T3.1; RWB-E1-030 sections 4, 12 and 16
description: The reconciliation compares the count of the ledger with the moves the run reports, but no source names the operation, the method, the path or the response fields of the rebalancing run record, and no field is named as the move count.
evidence: Legacy section 12 names JOB-06 and its output only; FSD P3 A2.17 and TSD P3 T3.1 name no run record object or endpoint; the ownership map holds no rebalance or run path for P3.
proposed: RWB-P3-E1030-CON publishes one read of the rebalancing run record for a business date, answering the move count and the case IDs of the moves, and rwb-decision consumes it as the second half of the reconciliation.

title: The message and the check name of the ledger count break are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6, FSD P7 A2.6 (MSG-P1-019, check REC-08); RWB-E1-030 section 14 and AC9
description: A difference between the count of the ledger and the moves of the run holds the report and lists the case for the data steward, but no source gives the message ID, the message text or the check name of that break.
evidence: Legacy MSG-P3-029 covers the queue depth check against the case list, a different check and a different owner; FSD P7 gives the lake reconciliation message MSG-P1-019 for check REC-08 only.
proposed: Add one message to the P7 message set for the ledger count break, and list it on the reconciliation break list of rwb-case with the business date, the two counts and the case of the missing move.

title: The actions payload keys and the assignment rule ID and version of the queue are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD P7 T3.1 (DF-DEC-014); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 and slide 27
description: The entry carries the reason REBALANCE, the assignment rule ID and rule version and the queue and owner identifiers in the actions payload, but no source names the keys of that payload, and no source gives the ASSIGNMENT rule rows, their rule ID form or their version label.
evidence: TSD P7 T3.1 types actions as jsonb and names no inner key; the design extract shows rule ID and version examples for ALLOCATION only, and no ASSIGNMENT row or version exists in the extracts.
proposed: Fix the actions keys against the decision-record library schema (reason, ruleId, ruleVersion, queueId, ownerUserId) and take the rule ID and version from the ASSIGNMENT row in force in the queue.

title: The decision filter value and the business date range of the count read are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD P7 appendix T-A API-P7-006 and T3.2 LOV-DECISION
description: The count of a business date is read on GET /decision-log with the decision, from and to parameters, but no source says which value the decision filter takes for a rebalance entry, nor how a business date maps to the from and to range.
evidence: TSD P7 T-A API-P7-006 lists decision, from and to without their values; T3.2 LOV-DECISION holds decision codes D5.1 to D9.3 and X1 to X7, while a rebalance entry is known by its final calls CASE_TRANSFERRED and OWNER_ASSIGNED.
proposed: Fix the decision filter as the final call of the entry (or add the rebalance decision code to LOV-DECISION), and read the business date as its first and last instant in from and to.
